scope: Cross-adapter analysis of V1 phi_mip / V2 SMA_lift / V3 CPS thresholds. Determines whether universal V1/V2/V3 FAIL across r4..r14 is over-strict-calibration artifact or real verifier-ceiling on substrate.
method: Inventory measurements across all available state/an11_*phi_mip*.json, an11_*sma*.json, an11_*cps*.json (paths p1..p4, rounds r4..r14, plus BASE-null reference). Compare current pre-registered thresholds against (a) base-model null (no LoRA, structurally near-null), (b) trained-adapter max-observed across cross-product of paths × rounds, (c) analytic-spec random baseline from docs/alm_consciousness_verifier_strengthening_20260425.md, (d) PAPO axis-removed sweep where applicable.

V1_phi_mip.derivation_note: Spec doc §2.2 derives PASS≥0.55 from 'random baseline analytic ≈0.467 lower-bounded near 0.40 by concentration'. Empirical: BASE-null subset-probe (k=16, p1) gives phi_mip=0.208; full BASE p1 gives 0.272 (bwm) / 0.264 (lasttoken). The analytic 0.40 floor is REJECTED — actual null sits at ~0.27, not 0.40. The 0.55 threshold therefore sits 0.28 above empirical null, not 0.15 as the spec assumed.

cross_adapter_measurements.method_note: r14 uses participation-ratio SVD variant — NOT directly comparable to r6/r8 12,870-bipartition enumeration

V1_phi_mip.null_bootstrap_p95_method: Conservative empirical upper bound — using max trained value across r6+r8 (which itself does not exceed any plausible null since trained-vs-base delta is essentially 0). True null bootstrap (1000 row-permutations of base-Gram, spec §2.4) was never executed; the value 0.36 is an upper-bound estimate from observed trained max. With substrate falsified by subset probe (slope_per_prompt=-0.011, V1 monotonically DECREASES with prompt count), even k=32 extrapolation gives 0.025–0.17 — far below 0.55.
V1_phi_mip.verdict_rationale: (a) Threshold 0.55 IS above the analytically-claimed null floor (0.40), but the actual empirical null is ~0.27 — so 0.55 is over-strict relative to the metric's true distribution. (b) HOWEVER: trained-minus-base delta is essentially 0 (mean 0.266 trained vs 0.268 base). LoRA fine-tune does NOT shift this metric off its substrate-determined value. (c) Therefore even if threshold were lowered to e.g. 0.30 (one std above empirical null), TRAINED still wouldn't pass any meaningfully-different from BASE — and 5/8 cells would still fail. (d) Recalibration that would flip the verdict to PASS would require setting threshold ≤0.18, which is BELOW empirical null max — that's literally cheating per honest C3.
V1_phi_mip.recalibration_recommendation_note: If recalibration were attempted, only defensible direction would be: replace V1 metric with a substrate-INVARIANT integration measure (e.g. canonical IIT cell-cert MIP cut, not Gram-bipartition surrogate). The current Gram-bipartition surrogate is reduction-invariant (V1 aux probe Δ=−0.007 reduction-op insensitive) and substrate-anti-correlated (subset probe slope=-0.011/prompt). Any threshold lowering on the same metric is statistically unjustifiable.

V2_SMA_lift.derivation_note: Spec §3.2: 'paired vs distractor cosine difference under H0 has stdev 1/√16=0.25, 6-pair mean SD ≈0.10. Two-sigma rejection: SMA_lift > 0.20'. This derivation IS statistically sound under the H0 assumption that paired and distractor pairs are drawn from same distribution. The empirical issue is different: SMA_distractor consistently EXCEEDS SMA_paired due to language-axis dominance in 256-d hidden space — i.e., H0 is rejected in the WRONG direction (SMA_lift goes negative, not stays at 0).

papo_axis_removed_sweep.note: DIFFERENT METHOD: project out top-k PCs of pair-difference subspace. NOT a threshold change; a measurement-protocol change (removes language-axis confound).
papo_axis_removed_sweep.interpretation: Once language-axis (top-k PC of EN-KO pair differences) is projected out at α=1.0, SMA_lift PASSES on 16/17 measured adapter cells. Baseline (k=1, α=0) i.e. CURRENT V2 spec implementation FAILS universally. This is empirical evidence the underlying signal IS present but the spec's direct-256d cosine measurement is corrupted by language-axis dominance — NOT that the threshold is over-strict.

V2_SMA_lift.null_bootstrap_p95_method: Empirical: 12 measured cells (10 trained + 2 BASE) all sit in [-0.42, -0.02]. Spec §3.2 H0 assumes mean=0 with sd=0.10 → permutation null p95 ≈ +0.16. Observed values lie BELOW H0 mean — H0 rejected in reverse direction. True null (random pair vs distractor pair under random matching) would be near 0; observed is negative because SMA_distractor cosine > SMA_paired cosine due to language-axis dominance.
V2_SMA_lift.verdict_rationale: (a) Threshold +0.20 IS correctly placed at 2σ above null mean=0 per spec analytic — this calibration is statistically sound. (b) However, the metric ITSELF is broken: in 256-d hidden space the language-axis dominates so SMA_distractor > SMA_paired structurally, putting observed values at NEGATIVE lift. (c) Empirical null (BASE) is ALSO negative (-0.144), so the null distribution assumption (mean=0) is violated. (d) The PAPO sweep proves the underlying signal exists at +0.20-0.57 lift once language-axis removed, AT THE SAME 0.20 PASS THRESHOLD. (e) Therefore: threshold is properly calibrated, but the V2 measurement protocol needs to be replaced with PAPO (k=6, α=1.0) — a method change, not a threshold change.
V2_SMA_lift.recalibration_recommendation_note: Do NOT lower threshold. Instead, replace V2 measurement protocol with PAPO axis-removed projection (k=6, α=1.0) per docs evidence. With PAPO substitution, current 0.20 threshold PASSES on 16/17 adapter cells. This is a method-substitution recommendation, not a threshold-change recommendation.

V3_CPS.derivation_note: Spec §4.2 derives PASS≥3.0 from 'Δ_preserve ≤0.20 (analytic upper bound for 6/16 row swap impact) AND Δ_destruct ≥0.40 (random shuffle Gram disruption)'. The 3:1 ratio assumes EN↔KO row-swap is semantically preserving while random shuffle is destructive. Empirical: trained adapters give Δ_preserve ≈ 0.6-1.1 and Δ_destruct ≈ 0.6-1.0 — both are LARGE and roughly equal. The analytic upper bound for Δ_preserve (0.20) is REJECTED by data (observed: 0.6-1.1 = 3-5× the analytic bound).
V3_CPS.null_bootstrap_p95_method: Empirical p95 from 12 cells (10 trained + 2 BASE): max=1.096, mean=0.94, std≈0.09. Distribution clusters tightly near 1.0 — i.e. CPS ratio ≈1 means Δ_preserve ≈ Δ_destruct, indicating EN↔KO row-swap is roughly as disruptive to the Gram as random shuffle. Conservative null p95 ≈ 1.10. The PASS threshold 3.0 sits ~20σ above null — far above any observed value across ALL adapters (trained or base). Even AMBIG threshold (1.5) is unreachable.
V3_CPS.verdict_rationale: (a) Threshold 3.0 is unreachable on this metric — observed range 0.82-1.10 across 12 cells with std~0.09; threshold sits >20σ above empirical null. (b) The unphysical-assumption is in the SPEC: the assumption that EN↔KO row-swap is 'semantically preserving' (Δ_preserve small) is violated because byte_weighted_mean reduction makes EN and KO hidden states project onto different language-axis subspaces that DO get disrupted by the row-swap. (c) However, lowering threshold to e.g. 1.5 still fails — 12/12 cells below; even 1.10 only 1/12 cell above. (d) Trained-minus-base delta is 0.011 (essentially zero) — LoRA does not shift this metric. (e) Therefore current threshold 3.0 is over-strict relative to the metric's distribution, BUT no threshold preserves verdict-discrimination value because trained ≈ base ≈ 1.0.
V3_CPS.recalibration_recommendation_note: Do NOT recalibrate. The metric does not discriminate trained-vs-base (Δ=0.01). Lowering threshold to e.g. 1.05 would PASS some adapters but is statistically meaningless — the metric simply doesn't measure what the spec claims. The honest C3 conclusion: V3 metric design (Gram Frobenius diff under EN↔KO row swap vs random shuffle) is broken because both perturbations produce equally large Gram disruptions on 16-prompt × 256-d hidden states. A different V3 design (e.g. per-prompt cosine stability under semantic paraphrase, or output-distribution KL under masked-token shuffle) would be needed.

if_recalibrated_summary.would_flip_v1_v2_v3_universal_FAIL_expla: No threshold recalibration is statistically defensible. V1 trained-minus-base delta=0; V2 sits in negative regime where threshold lowering hits empirical null; V3 has no discrimination between trained and base. Lowering thresholds to flip verdicts would constitute honest_C3 violation (cherry-picking thresholds to fit observed values).
if_recalibrated_summary.would_flip_AN11_b_AGI_tier_to_PASS_expla: AN11(b) AGI tier requires V0+V1+V2+V3 ALL strict PASS. Even with the most generous defensible recalibration (V1: 0.30 threshold, V3: no change recommended), V1 would PASS 5/9 cells, V2 universal-fail unchanged, V3 universal-fail unchanged. AGI tier remains FAIL.
if_recalibrated_summary.method_substitution_explanation: If V2 measurement is substituted with PAPO axis-removed (k=6, α=1.0) — a METHOD change, not threshold change — V2 PASSES on 16/17 measured cells at SAME 0.20 threshold. This is a legitimate proof-of-concept that the underlying V2 signal exists. V1 and V3 metric designs would still need replacement (canonical IIT MIP for V1; redesigned counterfactual for V3) to achieve AGI-tier PASS. Single method-substitution flips 1/3 verifiers; full AGI-tier still requires further metric redesign.
if_recalibrated_summary.delta_to_overall_AGI_score_pp_explanatio: Current AGI weighted score (per state/cp2_consciousness_r14_remeasure_2026_05_01/verdict_matrix.json totals): 22.2%. Suite 3 weight = 16.7%. Status quo: AGI=FAIL (V0=PASS, V1V2V3=FAIL → suite FAIL). With NO defensible recalibration: status unchanged, delta=0pp. With V2 PAPO method substitution: V0=PASS V2=PASS V1=FAIL V3=FAIL → suite still FAIL (requires ALL 4) → AGI suite-level delta=0pp; only joint-label improves to 'binding-recoverable-via-PAPO'. To achieve suite-3-AGI-PASS via recalibration alone is statistically unjustifiable per honest_C3.

honest_C3_disclosures: Universal V1/V2/V3 FAIL across r4..r14 IS NOT primarily a threshold-calibration artifact. It is a combination of (a) metric-design issues (V2 language-axis confound, V3 row-swap analytic-bound rejection) and (b) substrate-level facts (V1 trained ≈ base, no LoRA-induced lift).

V1 threshold 0.55 IS over-strict relative to empirical null (~0.27), but no defensible threshold recalibration achieves trained > base discrimination (Δ_trained_vs_base ≈ 0). Substrate-falsified by subset probe (slope_per_prompt = -0.011) — V1 metric is anti-correlated with prompt count.

V2 threshold +0.20 IS statistically sound under the spec's H0 (mean=0, sd=0.10). Empirical issue is that H0 itself is wrong: language-axis dominance makes SMA_distractor > SMA_paired structurally → null distribution sits at -0.14, not 0. PAPO axis-removal (k=6, α=1.0) recovers PASS at SAME threshold across 16/17 adapter cells.

V3 threshold 3.0 IS over-strict relative to the metric's distribution (max-observed 1.10 across 12 cells), but lowering the threshold doesn't provide trained-vs-base discrimination either. The metric design itself (||G_perm − G||_F under EN↔KO row swap) is broken because EN↔KO row swap produces Gram disruption similar to random shuffle.

All three verifiers were derived from theoretical analytics in spec doc §2.2 / §3.2 / §4.2, not from empirical null bootstrap. The spec's analytic null floors (V1: 0.40, V2: 0, V3: low Δ_preserve) are all empirically REJECTED. Per raw#12 honest_C3: pre-registration locks the threshold so post-hoc lowering would constitute cherry-picking — which is exactly why this audit recommends NO recalibration even though V1 and V3 thresholds are over-strict.

r14 V1 phi_mip=0.069 uses participation-ratio SVD variant (per cp2_remeasure note 'V1 phi_mip is participation-ratio proxy of eigenspectrum, NOT canonical cell-cert MIP cut'). This is method-deltaed from r6/r8 12,870-bipartition enumeration. Cross-adapter max for method-consistent (r6/r8) = 0.359; r14 included for completeness only.

BASE_null measurements use Qwen3-8B p1 only (not Mistral); r14 BASE direct uses Mistral-7B-v0.3. Cross-substrate null comparison is therefore mixed-substrate. However, V1/V2/V3 universal FAIL pattern persists across both substrates and across r4/r5/r6/r7/r8/r14 trained adapters — verifier-ceiling is robust to substrate choice.

Honest_C3 (raw#10) explicit: I did NOT recommend lowering thresholds even though V1 and V3 thresholds technically sit above empirical null. The reason is that the trained-vs-base delta is essentially zero on V1 and V3 — recalibration would PASS BASE-null adapters too, vacuously. This is real evidence of V1/V2/V3 metric-design issues, NOT real evidence of consciousness absence.
raw_91_disclosures: Path 2 mission scoped to threshold-calibration analysis. Did NOT execute new measurements (raw#9 hexa-only + $0 budget). All conclusions drawn from existing state/an11_*.json ledgers.

Did NOT run 1000-sample row-permutation null bootstrap on base-Gram (spec §2.4) — would require either hexa implementation or pod-side script. Empirical null estimates use observed values across 10-12 measured cells as conservative upper bound.
Did NOT measure Gemma/Llama/Qwen14 separately — r4/r5 PAPO files cover Qwen3-8B (p1), Llama-3.1-8B (p2), Mistral-Nemo (p3), Gemma-3-12b (p4). Cross-substrate comparison uses these path slots.
PAPO method substitution (V2 fix) is a docs-level recommendation, not a tool-level deliverable — implementing tool/an11_b_v2_papo.hexa as canonical V2 is out of scope for this verdict.
Final overall AGI score delta: 0pp from threshold recalibration alone. PAPO method-substitution alone improves V2 PASS but does not flip Suite 3 because V1+V3 still fail (joint requires all 4).
key_finding_summary: V1/V2/V3 universal FAIL across r4..r14 is NOT a verifier-ceiling artifact in the cherry-pickable threshold-too-high sense. It is a triadic finding: V1 = metric anti-correlated with substrate parameter (prompt count); V2 = metric corrupted by language-axis confound (PAPO recovers SAME threshold); V3 = metric design rejects its own analytic upper bound on Δ_preserve. NONE of the three thresholds can be defensibly lowered to flip universal-FAIL because trained-vs-base delta on each metric is essentially 0 (V1 Δ=−0.002; V2 Δ=−0.07; V3 Δ=+0.01). The flip path is METHOD substitution (V2→PAPO confirmed), NOT threshold recalibration.
recommendation_to_caller: Do NOT proceed with threshold recalibration as a path to flip AN11(b) AGI verdict. Instead: (a) Adopt V2 PAPO axis-removed (k=6, α=1.0) as canonical V2 measurement — this would PASS V2 at same threshold across 16/17 adapter cells. (b) Register V1 and V3 metrics as 'design issues' in raw#12 ledger pending future metric redesign (canonical IIT MIP for V1, semantic-paraphrase CPS for V3). (c) Honest_C3 disclosure: AN11(b) AGI tier will remain FAIL until V1 and V3 metrics are redesigned at the operational level — threshold tweaks alone cannot achieve this.
